newsitem.title: ITALY: Parliament gives go ahead to Italian reform push.
newsitem.headline: Parliament gives go ahead to Italian reform push.

text.p: Italy's lower house of parliament voted by an overwhelming margin on Wednesday in favour of creating a special commission to draft proposed constitutional reforms to end the country's instability.

The vote was the fourth and final ballot in six months of parliamentary wrangling on the plan. It leaves the 70-member commission, formed from both houses of parliament, just five months to come up with its blueprint for change.
The vote in the Chamber of Deputies in favour of the bicameral body was 534 to 70 with eight abstentions, Speaker Luciano Violante announced.
The governing centre-left coalition and the main opposition centre-right Freedom Alliance both backed the plan.

The commission's brief will be to propose changes to the system of government and parliament and the structure of the state laid down in the 1948 constitution. Its proposals will go back to parliament and then to a referendum.

Italy has had 54 governments since World War Two and three general elections since 1992 in the upheavals that followed the exposure of entrenched political corruption and the collapse of the old governing class.
